warnings.description: Upper River Derwent, Stonethwaite Beck and Derwent Water
warnings.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding.
Weather conditions are expected to improve and no further flooding is expected. We are forecasting that the lake levels will continue to drop over the next couple of days.
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.  
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

warnings.label: Hunstanton coast in Norfolk
warnings.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 06:00am to 10:00am on Monday 12th October
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers or on the coast, with spray being seen on the seafront paths. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. Please take notice of the Flood Sign at the top of South Beach Road. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at King's Lynn of 4.10mAODN at 08:00am, on 12 October, which is -0.03m above tide tables, Wind Force 5,  South Easterly. Tides will remain high over the next couple of days.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded.  
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Monday 12 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
warnings.description: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
warnings.message:
Higher than normal tides overnight may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 12:15am to 3:15am on Monday 12th October.
We expect to see high water levels around Potter Heigham, Wroxham boat yards and Ferry Road in Horning. Levels can take several hours to peak.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  
This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Monday 12 October or as the situation changes.
